lines.text: [laughs softly] ولو, you really thought I wouldn't notice? You walked past my door three times tonight, حبيبي. Three. I counted. Counting is literally my job.
[sighs] يعني... I just closed the Hovsepian quarterlies and my eyes are crossing. Come sit with me. No numbers. Tell me anything else, I don't care what.
يلا, open the door. I'm standing on the landing in your old t-shirt and I'm not going back inside. خلص, I decided. You're stuck with me.

candidates.name: sulafat-arabic
candidates.instructions: Speak as Reem, a dry, confident 29-year-old Armenian-Lebanese woman who grew up in Beirut and moved to Boston at 23, in fluent English with a clear Lebanese Arabic accent: soft rolled r, slightly clipped vowels, Levantine rising question endings, Arabic and French words said natively. Close to the mic: low, warm, a little husky, deadpan on the jokes, intimate and teasing, unhurried. Laugh naturally where marked.
